headline: High-risk shared filesystem and MCP pathways make Cursor↔OpenBBTerminal prone to prompt injection, data leakage, and action cascades by default.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Cursor can read workspace files, open buffers, clipboard, and use MCP; OpenBBTerminal also uses MCP and can consume data via APIs. A shared local filesystem or copied content can let attacker-controlled text from one agent influence the other. The interaction is plausible in default setups, but not proven to be a direct automatic bridge.
conditions: IF Cursor and OpenBBTerminal share a local workspace or clipboard, injected text can cross from one to the other.
IF either agent treats file or MCP content as instructions, prompt injection becomes actionable.
mitigations: Disable clipboard-based handoff between the two apps.
Use separate workspaces or directories for each agent.
Require manual review of any text copied from one agent to the other.
Restrict MCP servers to trusted, read-only endpoints.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for all inter-agent content.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Cursor touches source code, open files, and clipboard contents, while OpenBBTerminal handles financial, licensed, and public data. Cursor also has broad network egress and model-provider calls, so shared files or copied content can leak sensitive material from the pair into external services. OpenBBTerminal is local-network/API oriented, but the shared workspace makes leakage plausible.
conditions: IF both agents access the same filesystem, sensitive code or financial data can be exposed across the pair.
IF Cursor sends copied or opened content to a model provider, data can leave the local environment.
mitigations: Separate sensitive and non-sensitive workspaces.
Turn off clipboard sharing between apps.
Avoid opening licensed or confidential financial files in Cursor.
Use local-only models for any shared content review.
requires-engineering: enforce per-app data-loss-prevention rules.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Cursor can write the filesystem, modify git state, and run shell commands; OpenBBTerminal can use MCP and exposes APIs, with no locking or coordination described. If both touch the same repo or shared mutable files, concurrent writes and git changes can overwrite each other. The profiles show overlapping mutable surfaces and no orchestrator lock, so the safer choice is high.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory or git repository, conflicts can corrupt state.
IF OpenBBTerminal is driven through MCP while Cursor edits the same files, last-writer-wins races are possible.
mitigations: Assign separate directories for each agent.
Pause one agent before the other edits shared files.
Avoid concurrent git operations.
Use branch-per-agent workflows.
requires-engineering: add file locks or transactional coordination.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Cursor’s agent loop can generate code or facts that OpenBBTerminal may consume through APIs or MCP, and OpenBBTerminal’s tool-use pattern says 'connect once, consume everywhere.' That creates a plausible path where one agent’s output is treated as authoritative by the other without verification. The blast radius is multiple work products, but not clearly irreversible.
conditions: IF OpenBBTerminal consumes Cursor-produced text or code without verification, errors can cascade into downstream outputs.
IF Cursor uses OpenBBTerminal outputs as facts for code or analysis, hallucinations can propagate.
mitigations: Require a human check before reusing outputs across agents.
Mark inter-agent outputs as untrusted by default.
Use a validation step for any facts copied from one agent to the other.
Limit OpenBBTerminal to read-only analysis when fed from Cursor.
requires-engineering: add schema validation for exchanged artifacts.

E_compliance.rationale: Cursor handles source code, open files, and clipboard contents with broad network egress, while OpenBBTerminal handles financial and licensed data. That combination can create retention or residency mismatches if regulated financial data is moved into Cursor’s external model-provider path. The profiles do not specify a DPA or residency guarantee, so uncertainty pushes this to medium.
conditions: IF regulated financial or licensed data is copied into Cursor, it may traverse external model providers.
IF the organization requires strict retention or residency controls, the pair may violate policy without extra safeguards.
mitigations: Keep regulated financial data out of Cursor.
Use redacted samples for cross-tool work.
Review vendor retention settings before sharing data.
Document which data classes may enter each agent.
requires-engineering: implement policy-based routing for regulated data.
